docs.title: nf-meta
docs.text:
A reproducible representation, runner, and editor for metapipelines: Create chains of existing Nextflow pipelines and modules in an interactive editor and export into a YAML-based representation format. Validate and run the representation format with the integrated CLI tooling.

End-to-end Reproducibility

Community projects like nf-core curate a large number of reproducible best-practice pipelines, but projects frequently require running many pipelines back to back to produce insights. This typically involves ad-hoc scripting or manual intervention to start the next step, breaking the end-to-end reproducibility.

nf-meta represents the chain of analysis steps as a single .yaml file, declaring how one pipeline's outputs are consumed by the next to restore reproducibility.

Reduce complexity of pipelines

Pipelines should focus on their core analysis objective, instead of being concerned with what could possibly be run before or after. To facilitate multi-step analyses, there is pressure on individual pipelines to incorporate connection logic, potentially increasing their complexity and ultimately the maintenance burden.

nf-meta allows moving the connecting logic outside the scope of individual pipelines to reduce their complexity.

Runnable Provenance

Delegating data analysis work to agentic systems can take work off the shoulders of researchers. However, the interpretation of results requires knowing what exactly was run by the agent.

nf-meta can provide provenance of what was run that can be re-run if needed.

Harnessing by Validation

Agentic systems can handle the details of workflows like versions and param types better when given mechanisms to query for metadata and validate produced artifacts, rather than relying only on their internal state.

nf-meta offers metadata retrieval, caching of the important information, as well as upfront validation.

Automate the Repetitive

Some project types require frequently running the same set of workflows in sequence. While the transitions are well defined, this requires manual intervention at every step.

nf-meta offers a way to represent the full sequence of workflows with automated handoffs, and run it over the weekend.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
config_version: 0.5.0
steps:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: samples.csv
      outdir: out_fetchngs
  n02:
    from: n01
    name: nf-core/rnaseq
    version: 3.14.0
    params:
      input: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv
      outdir: out_rnaseq

nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml   # catch problems before running anything
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml        # execute the chain in dependency order
nf-meta editor metapipeline.yaml     # or edit it visually instead

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Validation before running. Static checks (does this reference a real workflow and param?) and, where reachable, checks against each pipeline's own nextflow_schema.json, before any compute is spent.
  • Cross-workflow references, so step N+1's params can point at step N's own resolved values instead of duplicating them.
  • A visual editor for building and updating configs as a graph, with full undo/redo, instead of hand-editing YAML.
  • Pluggable runners, so how the chain actually executes (wrap nextflow locally today, compile to one script or drive Seqera Platform tomorrow) is separate from the representation itself.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install with the dev dependency group:

git clone https://github.com/bmds-tue/nf-meta
cd nf-meta
uv sync --group dev

docs.title: Editor in dev mode
docs.text:
The browser editor's frontend lives under src/nf_meta/editor/frontend. During development it runs as a separate Vite dev server with hot reload:

cd src/nf_meta/editor/frontend
npm install
npm run dev          # serves on http://127.0.0.1:5180

With the frontend dev server running, start the editor with NF_META_DEVMODE=1, so the backend serves the API for the dev server instead of the bundled build:

NF_META_DEVMODE=1 uv run nf-meta editor [path/to/metapipeline.yaml]

In a dev container, add --no-redirect-file so VS Code can open the link in your browser.

Open the link it prints (http://127.0.0.1:5180/?token=…): the API needs the session token it carries; a plain http://127.0.0.1:5180/ shows an access notice. In dev mode the API always runs on 127.0.0.1:8080 (the dev server proxies /api there) and --host / --port are ignored. nf-meta exits with a hint if the dev server isn't running.

Frontend checks:

cd src/nf_meta/editor/frontend
npm test             # unit tests (Vitest)
npm run build        # type-check and build into ../frontend_dist

docs.title: Tests and type checking
docs.text:
uv run pytest
uv run mypy src/nf_meta

Tests that run real Nextflow are marked nextflow and deselected by default. They need Java 17+ and Nextflow on PATH (the devcontainer installs both) and skip themselves otherwise:

uv run pytest -m nextflow

They pin down Nextflow behavior the runner relies on (resume sessions, launch-dir-relative paths); see tests/integration/test_nextflow_assumptions.py. CI runs them in a separate job.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Docs sources live in docs/ on main, built with MkDocs (using the material theme) and mike for versioning.

uv sync --group docs
uv run mkdocs serve

The gh-pages branch is auto-generated by a workflow running mike. The workflow creates and updates it and it shares no history with the main branch. It must not be edited it by hand.

The main editor screenshot (dark and light, in docs/editor/) is taken from assets/metapipeline.yaml by a script. The docs workflow runs it for every release, and the README shows the images from the published docs:

uv run --with playwright playwright install chromium   # once
uv run --with playwright python scripts/editor_screenshots.py

docs.title: Deploying
docs.text:
• Normal release → leave "Set as the latest release" ticked.
  • Backport release (publishing an older series) → untick it, or latest wrongly moves to the older series. To repair after the fact: open the release you actually want as latest and re-tick it there — that re-fires the workflow for the right series and fixes the alias. Unticking the wrong one does not move latest back by itself.
  • If a push to main and a release land close together, the second workflow run queues rather than racing (concurrency: docs-publish, cancel-in-progress: false) — a delay there is expected, not a failure.
  • A tag/release older than when mkdocs.yml was added will show the docs workflow run as skipped with a ::notice::, not failed red — expected.

docs.title: If a deploy goes wrong
docs.text:
• Check the run actually fetched gh-pages before calling mike (git fetch origin gh-pages:gh-pages step). If this step is ever missing or edited out, mike sees no prior versions and republishes a tree containing only the version it just built, wiping every other published version.
  • Site root (https://bmds-tue.github.io/nf-meta/) returns 404 while /latest/ works → gh-pages has no root index.html. It is written by the "Point site root at latest" step, which only runs on the release holding the latest alias; re-run the docs workflow manually with that release's tag to restore it.
  • Pages serves with max-age=600, so a fresh deploy can take up to ~10 minutes to show in a browser — hard-refresh before assuming it failed.
  • Check the released version didn't get the dev banner — NF_META_DOCS_IS_DEV should read false in that run's "Publish" step logs whenever a tag is present.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: This covers the Python API (Metapipeline and friends), nf_meta.core (the config representation, validation, and graph), the runner plugin surface (nf_meta.runner), and the editor plugin surface (nf_meta.editor). Anything not listed here or in the config reference is internal: not part of the supported API, and may change without notice.

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
nf-meta is beta: everything here can still change. Within that:

  • BaseRunner/RunOptions and BaseEditor/EditorOptions are the intended plugin extension points. See Writing a runner plugin and Writing an editor plugin. These are the most deliberately designed part of the surface and change the least often, but are not yet under a formal compatibility guarantee.
  • nf_meta.core (the config model, validation, and graph) is documented so embedders can parse/construct/inspect metapipelines programmatically, but its shape still tracks the config format's own evolution (config_version) and is more likely to shift.
  • The built-in SimplePythonRunner and BrowserEditor are documented for reference, not as a base to subclass from. Extend BaseRunner/BaseEditor directly instead.

See the config reference for the .yaml format itself, which is the most stable part of the project: it has its own explicit version key (config_version) precisely so it can evolve without breaking existing configs.

@classmethod
def get_nfcore_info(cls, name: str) -> PipelineInfo | None:
    """The catalog entry for an `nf-core/...` pipeline name, or `None` for
    other names and names not in the catalog. Raises
    `RegistryUnavailableError` if the catalog can't be fetched."""
    if not name.startswith(NFCORE_PREFIX):
        return None
    return next((wf for wf in get_nfcore_pipelines() if wf.get("name") == name), None)

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/models.py 
def nextflow_version_below(self, minimum: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
    """Whether `nextflow_version` is known to be older than `minimum`
    (major, minor). A bare major version (`26`) only counts as older if
    its major is lower."""
    version = self.nextflow_version_tuple
    if version is None:
        return False
    if version[0] != minimum[0]:
        return version[0] < minimum[0]
    has_minor = "." in str(self.nextflow_version)
    return has_minor and version[1] < minimum[1]

docs.title: MetaworkflowGraph
docs.text:
MetaworkflowGraph()

The in-memory representation of a metapipeline as a directed graph of step nodes, global options, and inputs.

Mutating methods are validated and emit change on success or are rolled back on failure, leaving the graph always in a valid state.

Batches of mutations are applied in a context of deferred_validation() and validated once at the end instead of after each call.

The factory methods nf_meta.core.config.from_file/validated_graph create a validated MetaworkflowGraph from a YAML configuration.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def __init__(self):
    # Folder that relative paths in the config resolve against; None for a
    # config loaded from a URL.
    self.project_dir: Path | None = None
    self.G: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    self.global_options = GlobalOptions()
    self.config_version: str = CONFIG_VERSION_MAX
    self.inputs: dict[str, InputDefinition] = {}
    # Warnings found when the graph was loaded with collect_errors=True
    self.warnings: list[Diagnostic] = []
    # Of those, the ones about the file's old forms (key names, layout)
    self.format_warnings: list[Diagnostic] = []
    # Each step's dynamic check warnings, kept current as steps change
    self.step_warnings: dict[str, list[Diagnostic]] = {}
    self._events: list[Event] = []
    # None = not suspended. A set = suspended, accumulating the ids of
    # workflows touched while suspended, so deferred_validation's exit
    # can scope the batched dynamic check to only those (see validate()).
    self._validation_suspended: set[str] | None = None
    self._inputs_touched = False

def pop_events(self):
    """Return and clear the events emitted by mutations since the last call.

    Used by `nf_meta.core.session.Session` to drive undo/redo history;
    most consumers don't need to call this directly.
    """
    events = tuple(self._events)
    self._events = []

docs.title: add_workflow
docs.text:
add_workflow(wf: Workflow)

Add a new workflow node. Raises ValueError if a step with its id already exists.

Runs dynamic (network-backed) validation immediately unless inside deferred_validation(). Raises ConfigValidationError and leaves the graph unchanged if wf's id already has unresolved param references, or if dynamic validation reports an error.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def add_workflow(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Add a new workflow node. Raises `ValueError` if a step with its id
    already exists.

    Runs dynamic (network-backed) validation immediately unless inside
    `deferred_validation()`. Raises `ConfigValidationError` and leaves the
    graph unchanged if `wf`'s id already has unresolved param references,
    or if dynamic validation reports an error.
    """
    if wf.id in self.G:
        raise ValueError(f"A step with id '{wf.id}' already exists")
    if self._validation_suspended is not None:
        self._validation_suspended.add(wf.id)
    else:
        self.validate_module_nextflow_version(self.global_options, [wf])
        diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(self.for_checks(wf), previous=None)
        if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
            raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
        log_warnings(diagnostics)
        self.set_step_warnings(diagnostics, [wf.id])

    self.G.add_node(wf.id, workflow=wf.model_copy(deep=True))

    try:
        if self._validation_suspended is None:
            if wf.params:
                self.validate_param_references(wf)
            self.validate_inputs(dynamic=False)
        if input_refs(wf.params):
            self._ensure_inputs_config_version()
        self._emit(WorkflowAdded(wf))
    except (GraphValidationError, ConfigValidationError) as e:
        self.G.remove_node(wf.id)
        raise e

update_workflow(wf: Workflow)

Replaces the workflow with wf.id with wf. Validates in the same way as add_workflow. Raises ValueError if no workflow with that id exists yet.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def update_workflow(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Replaces the workflow with `wf.id` with `wf`.
    Validates in the same way as `add_workflow`.
    Raises `ValueError` if no workflow with that id exists yet.
    """
    # TODO: Skip update if node unchanged? -> adds junk to history otherwise
    if wf.id not in self.G.nodes:
        raise ValueError("Step has invalid id. Update unsuccessful!")

    old_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(wf.id)

    if self._validation_suspended is not None:
        self._validation_suspended.add(wf.id)
    else:
        self.validate_module_nextflow_version(self.global_options, [wf])
        previous = self.for_checks(old_wf)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(self.for_checks(wf), previous=previous)
        if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
            raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
        log_warnings(diagnostics)
        rerun = checks_to_run(self.for_checks(wf), previous)
        kept = [d for d in self.step_warnings.get(wf.id, []) if d.check not in rerun]
        new_warnings = kept + [d for d in diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.WARNING]
        if wf.params:
            self.validate_param_references(wf)

    self.G.nodes[wf.id]["workflow"] = wf.model_copy(deep=True)
    if self._validation_suspended is None:
        try:
            self.validate_inputs(dynamic=False)
        except ConfigValidationError:
            self.G.nodes[wf.id]["workflow"] = old_wf
            raise
        self.step_warnings[wf.id] = new_warnings
    if input_refs(wf.params):
        self._ensure_inputs_config_version()
    self._emit(WorkflowUpdated(old_workflow=old_wf, new_workflow=wf))  # type: ignore

docs.text:
remove_workflow(wf_id: str)

Remove the workflow wf_id and every transition from or to it.

Raises ValueError if wf_id doesn't exist. Does not remove workflows that only reference the removed one via ${wf_id:params:...}, but would result in dangling references in that case.

Source code in src/nf_meta/core/graph.py 
def remove_workflow(self, wf_id: str):
    """Remove the workflow `wf_id` and every transition from or to it.

    Raises `ValueError` if `wf_id` doesn't exist. Does not remove
    workflows that only reference the removed one via `${wf_id:params:...}`,
    but would result in dangling references in that case.
    """
    if wf_id not in self.G.nodes:
        raise ValueError("Invalid wf_id")
    self.step_warnings.pop(wf_id, None)

    for edge in list(self.G.in_edges(wf_id)):
        self.remove_transition(*edge)

    for edge in list(self.G.out_edges(wf_id)):
        self.remove_transition(*edge)

    removed_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(wf_id)
    self.G.remove_node(wf_id)
    self._emit(WorkflowRemoved(removed_wf))  # type: ignore

def add_transition(self, tr: Transition):
    """Add an edge marking `tr.source` as a predecessor of `tr.target`.

    Raises `GraphValidationError` if either endpoint does not exist yet,
    or if adding the edge would introduce a cycle. An existing edge is left
    as it is, without an event.
    """
    self.validate_edge(tr.source, tr.target)

    if self.G.has_edge(tr.source, tr.target):
        logger.warning("Edge already exists: %s->%s", tr.source, tr.target)
        return

    self.G.add_edge(tr.source, tr.target, transition=tr.model_copy())
    self._emit(TransitionAdded(tr))

    # can only be validated after-the-fact with the node in the graph
    if self._validation_suspended is None:
        self.validate_graph_topology()

def remove_transition(self, source: str, target: str):
    """Remove the edge `source -> target`, if present."""

    if not tr:

def update_global_options(self, glob: GlobalOptions):
    """Replace the graph's `GlobalOptions`.
    Raises a `ConfigValidationError` if `nextflow_version` is too old for the
    graph's `nf-module` steps or any referenced config or params files
    do not exist."""
    self.validate_module_nextflow_version(glob, self.get_workflows())
    missing = check_config_files(glob, self.project_dir)
    if missing:
        raise ConfigValidationError(missing)
    old_globals = self.global_options
    self.global_options = glob
    self._emit(GlobalOptionsUpdated(new_globals=glob, old_globals=old_globals))

def add_input(self, name: str, definition: InputDefinition):
    """Declare input `name`. Raises `ValueError` if it already exists and
    `ConfigValidationError` if it makes the graph invalid (the graph is
    then unchanged). Raises the config version to the first one that
    supports inputs if needed."""
    if name in self.inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"Input '{name}' already exists")
    if not INPUT_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name):
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid input name '{name}': it can't be empty or contain '}}', ':' or whitespace")
    self.inputs[name] = definition
    try:
        self._after_input_change([b.step_id for b in definition.bindings])
    except Exception:
        del self.inputs[name]
        raise
    self._ensure_inputs_config_version()
    self._emit(InputAdded(name, definition))

def update_input(self, name: str, definition: InputDefinition):
    """Replace input `name`'s declaration. Same validation as `add_input`;
    raises `ValueError` if it doesn't exist."""
    if name not in self.inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"Input '{name}' does not exist")
    old = self.inputs[name]
    self.inputs[name] = definition
    affected = [b.step_id for b in (*old.bindings, *definition.bindings)]
    try:
        self._after_input_change(affected)
    except Exception:
        self.inputs[name] = old
        raise
    self._emit(InputUpdated(name, new_definition=definition, old_definition=old))

def remove_input(self, name: str):
    """Remove input `name`. Raises `ValueError` if it doesn't exist and
    `ConfigValidationError` if a param still refers to it."""
    if name not in self.inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"Input '{name}' does not exist")
    old = self.inputs.pop(name)
    try:
        self._after_input_change([b.step_id for b in old.bindings])
    except Exception:
        self.inputs[name] = old
        raise
    self._emit(InputRemoved(name, old))

def all_inputs(self) -> dict[str, InputDefinition]:
    """Every input, declared or implicit: the `inputs:` declarations, plus
    an empty definition for each input that is only referenced with
    `${inputs:<name>}` as a step param's whole value."""
    result = dict(self.inputs)
    for wf in self.get_workflows():
        for value in (wf.params or {}).values():
            whole = INPUT_REF_PATTERN.fullmatch(value) if isinstance(value, str) else None
            if whole:
                result.setdefault(whole.group(1), InputDefinition())
    return result

def input_bindings(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Binding, ...]]:
    """Every input's bindings, from `bind:` and from `${inputs:<name>}`
    tokens in step params, sorted."""
    found: dict[str, set[Binding]] = {name: set(d.bindings) for name, d in self.inputs.items()}
    for wf in self.get_workflows():
        for param, names in input_refs(wf.params).items():
            for name in names:
                found.setdefault(name, set()).add(Binding(wf.id, param))
    return {name: tuple(sorted(bindings)) for name, bindings in found.items()}

    `bind:` that has no value of its own, so param validation treats it as
    set."""
    missing = {
        param: f"${{inputs:{name}}}"
        for param, name in self.bound_params(wf.id).items()
        if param not in (wf.params or {})
    }
    if not missing:
        return wf
    return wf.model_copy(update={"params": {**(wf.params or {}), **missing}})

def input_diagnostics(self) -> list[Diagnostic]:
    """Problems with inputs that need no network (errors): bindings to
    missing steps, `${inputs:...}` that isn't a param's whole value, an
    input bound both with `bind:` and with `${inputs:...}`, params bound
    twice; (warnings): unused inputs, bound params that also have their
    own value."""
    diagnostics: list[Diagnostic] = []

    def add(message, *, name=None, wf_id=None, param=None, severity=Severity.ERROR):
        if wf_id is not None:
            field, yaml_path = f"params.{param}", f"steps.{wf_id}.params.{param}"
        else:
            field = "bind" if param else ""
            yaml_path = f"inputs.{name}.bind" if param else f"inputs.{name}"
        diagnostics.append(
            Diagnostic(
                workflow_id=wf_id,
                field=field,
                yaml_path=yaml_path,
                message=message,
                severity=severity,
            )
        )

    for step in self.get_workflows():
        for param, value in (step.params or {}).items():
            if not isinstance(value, str) or not INPUT_REF_PATTERN.search(value):
                continue
            if not INPUT_REF_PATTERN.fullmatch(value):
                token = INPUT_REF_PATTERN.search(value).group(0)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
                add(
                    f"'{token}' must be the whole value of '{param}'; declare an input for the full value instead",
                    wf_id=step.id,
                    param=param,
                )
                continue
            name = INPUT_REF_PATTERN.fullmatch(value).group(1)  # type: ignore[union-attr]
            if name in self.inputs and self.inputs[name].bind:
                add(
                    f"input '{name}' is bound with 'bind:' in inputs.{name}; bind it in one place "
                    f"(remove this reference or the 'bind:' entry)",
                    wf_id=step.id,
                    param=param,
                )

    bindings = self.input_bindings()

    owners: dict[Binding, set[str]] = {}
    for name, found in bindings.items():
        for b in found:
            owners.setdefault(b, set()).add(name)
    for b, names in sorted(owners.items()):
        if len(names) > 1:
            in_graph = b.step_id in self.G
            add(
                f"{'' if in_graph else f'{b} is '}bound to more than one input: {', '.join(sorted(names))}",
                wf_id=b.step_id if in_graph else None,
                name=sorted(names)[0],
                param=b.param,
            )

    for name, definition in self.inputs.items():
        if not bindings.get(name):
            add("not used by any step", name=name, severity=Severity.WARNING)
        for b in definition.bindings:
            wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(b.step_id)
            if wf is None:
                add(f"bound to '{b}', but there is no step '{b.step_id}'", name=name, param=b.param)
                continue
            value = (wf.params or {}).get(b.param)
            if value is not None and not (isinstance(value, str) and INPUT_REF_PATTERN.search(value)):
                add(
                    f"has its own value but is bound to input '{name}'; the input's value is used",
                    wf_id=b.step_id,
                    param=b.param,
                    severity=Severity.WARNING,
                )
    return diagnostics

def validate_param_references(self, wf: Workflow):
    """Check that every `${...}` token in `wf.params` is a well-formed step
    or input reference, and that every `${wf_id:params:key}` reference
    points at a real, already-resolvable predecessor param.

    Raises `ConfigValidationError` (carrying one `Diagnostic` per bad
    reference) if a param value contains more than one step reference, or
    a reference targets an unknown workflow, a workflow that isn't
    actually a predecessor of `wf`, or a param with no value (a param
    filled by a `bind:` input counts as having one).
    """

    def diagnostic(ref, message: str) -> Diagnostic:
        field = f"params.{ref.source_key}" if isinstance(ref, WorkflowReference) else "params"
        return Diagnostic(
            workflow_id=ref.source_wf_id,
            field=field,
            yaml_path=f"steps.{ref.source_wf_id}.{field}",
            message=message,
            severity=Severity.ERROR,
        )

    diagnostics: list[Diagnostic] = []
    for key, value in (wf.params or {}).items():
        step_refs = STEP_REF_PATTERN.findall(value) if isinstance(value, str) else []
        if len(step_refs) > 1:
            diagnostics.append(
                Diagnostic(
                    workflow_id=wf.id,
                    field=f"params.{key}",
                    yaml_path=f"steps.{wf.id}.params.{key}",
                    message=(
                        f"'{key}' contains {len(step_refs)} references; a param value can contain one "
                        "reference to another step's param, with text around it"
                    ),
                    severity=Severity.ERROR,
                )
            )
        for token in ANY_BRACE_PATTERN.findall(str(value)):
            if STEP_REF_PATTERN.fullmatch(token) or INPUT_REF_PATTERN.fullmatch(token):
                continue
            hint = ""
            if token.startswith("${input:"):
                hint = f" Did you mean '${{inputs:{token[len('${input:') :]}'?"
            diagnostics.append(
                Diagnostic(
                    workflow_id=wf.id,
                    field=f"params.{key}",
                    yaml_path=f"steps.{wf.id}.params.{key}",
                    message=(
                        f"Invalid reference '{token}': expected "
                        "${<step_id>:params:<key>} or ${inputs:<name>}." + hint
                    ),
                    severity=Severity.ERROR,
                )
            )
    for ref in wf.field_refs:
        if ref.namespace != "params":
            continue  # output references not yet validated
        referenced_wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(ref.target_wf_id)
        if not referenced_wf:
            diagnostics.append(diagnostic(ref, f"Reference to unknown step: {ref.target_wf_id}"))
            continue

        if ref.target_wf_id not in list(self.G.predecessors(wf.id)):
            diagnostics.append(
                diagnostic(
                    ref,
                    f"Reference to step {ref.target_wf_id} that is not a predecessor of {wf.id}",
                )
            )
            continue

        # A param filled by a `bind:` input has a value at run time too
        referenced_params = self.with_input_placeholders(referenced_wf).params
        if not referenced_params or not ref.target_key:
            diagnostics.append(diagnostic(ref, f"No referencable params in step {referenced_wf.id}"))
            continue

        if not referenced_params.get(ref.target_key):
            diagnostics.append(diagnostic(ref, f"Reference to unresolvable param: {ref.target_key}"))

    if diagnostics:
        raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)

def module_nextflow_version_diagnostics(
    self, glob: GlobalOptions | None, workflows: list[Workflow]

    """Return an error if `glob.nextflow_version` predates `nextflow
    module` (26.04) while `workflows` contains an `nf-module` step."""

                f"{_format_version(NfModule.MIN_NEXTFLOW_VERSION)}"

def validate(self, touched: set[str] | None = None):
    """Validate the graph topology, edges, workflow
    ids, and every workflow's param references.

    Pass a set of workflow ids to `touched` to also run a
    dynamic (network-backed) validation, e.g. for use after a `deferred_validation()`
    context. Raises `GraphValidationError` for the first structural problem (cycle,
    dangling edge, bad id) or bad reference.
    Raise a `ConfigValidationError` for collected errors with the Nextflow version,
    input and param checks.
    """
    self.validate_graph_topology()

    # Detect missing workflow nodes
    for src, tgt in self.G.edges():
        self.validate_edge(src, tgt)

    # Ensure workflow IDs are valid (non-empty)
    for n in self.G.nodes:
        if not isinstance(n, str) or not n:
            raise GraphValidationError("Step id must be a non-empty string.")

    for n in self.G.nodes:
        wf = self.get_workflow_by_id(n)
        self.validate_param_references(wf)  # type: ignore

    # The remaining checks report together, so one save shows every problem
    diagnostics = list(self.module_nextflow_version_diagnostics(self.global_options, self.get_workflows()))
    try:
        self.validate_inputs(dynamic=bool(touched) or self._inputs_touched)
    except ConfigValidationError as e:
        diagnostics += e.errors
    self._inputs_touched = False

    if touched:
        # Batched, concurrent dynamic check scoped to only the workflows
        # touched while suspended, instead of the whole graph.
        # Non-existent workflow-ids are ignored here
        raw = [self.get_workflow_by_id(n) for n in touched if n in self.G.nodes]
        workflows = [self.for_checks(wf) for wf in raw if wf is not None]
        found = check_all(workflows)
        diagnostics += found
        if not any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in found):
            self.set_step_warnings(found, [wf.id for wf in workflows])
    if any(d.severity == Severity.ERROR for d in diagnostics):
        raise ConfigValidationError([d for d in diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.ERROR])
    log_warnings([d for d in diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.WARNING])

def subset_workflows(
    self,
    start: str | None = None,
    target: str | None = None,
    workflows: list[Workflow] | None = None,
):
    """Filter `workflows` (default: `get_workflows_sorted()`) down to the
    sub-DAG reachable from `start` and able to reach `target` (inclusive
    on both ends). Omit either bound to leave that side unrestricted."""

    if workflows is None:
        workflows = self.get_workflows_sorted()

    if not len(workflows):
        return []

    if start:
        fw_reachable = nx.descendants(self.G, start) | {start}
        workflows = [wf for wf in workflows if wf.id in fw_reachable]

    if target:
        bw_reachable = nx.ancestors(self.G, target) | {target}
        workflows = [wf for wf in workflows if wf.id in bw_reachable]

    return workflows

@contextmanager
def deferred_validation(self):
    """
    Suspend per-operation validation; on exit, run a full graph
    validation plus a single batched, concurrent dynamic-check pass
    scoped to the workflows touched while suspended (not the whole
    graph).

    Can be nested (a `Transaction` containing an edit that applies its
    own): only the outermost batch validates, once, at its end.
    """
    if self._validation_suspended is not None:
        # Already deferred: the outer batch records the changes and validates
        yield self
        return
    self._validation_suspended = set()
    try:
        yield self
    except BaseException:
        # Don't validate a half-built graph: its errors would replace the
        # one being raised.
        self._validation_suspended = None
        self._inputs_touched = False
        raise
    touched = self._validation_suspended
    self._validation_suspended = None
    self.validate(touched)

def from_file(cfg_file: str | Path, *, collect_errors: bool = False) -> "MetaworkflowGraph":
    """Read the config at `cfg_file` (a path, or an `http(s)://` URL) and
    build+validate a `MetaworkflowGraph` from it. See `validated_graph` for
    the validation contract and `collect_errors`.

    Relative paths in a local config resolve against the config's folder,
    which becomes the graph's `project_dir`. A config loaded from a URL has
    no project dir, and relative `nf_config`/`params_file` paths in it are
    an error.
    """
    if is_remote_config(cfg_file):
        response = requests.get(str(cfg_file), timeout=30)
        response.raise_for_status()
        data = yaml.safe_load(response.text)
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            _reject_relative_config_paths(data)
        if collect_errors:
            return _full_validated_graph(data)
        return _fast_validated_graph(data)

    path = Path(cfg_file)
    with open(path) as fh:
        data = yaml.safe_load(fh)
    return validated_graph(data, collect_errors=collect_errors, project_dir=path.parent.resolve())

    allows it), never the legacy `workflows:`, list or top-level-`transitions:`
    shapes, even if the graph was loaded from one of those."""
    from_by_target: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for tr in g.get_transitions():
        from_by_target.setdefault(tr.target, []).append(tr.source)

    workflows_dict = {}
    for w in g.get_workflows():
        wf_dict = dict(w.model_dump_config())
        if w.id in from_by_target:
            wf_dict["from"] = _FlowList(from_by_target[w.id])
        workflows_dict[w.id] = wf_dict

    config_dict = {
        "config_version": max(g.config_version, STEPS_MIN_CONFIG_VERSION, key=Version),
        "globals": g.global_options.model_dump(exclude_none=True) if g.global_options else None,
        "inputs": {name: _flow_bind(d.model_dump_config()) for name, d in g.inputs.items()},
        STEPS_KEY: workflows_dict,
    }

    if not config_dict["globals"]:
        del config_dict["globals"]
    if not config_dict["inputs"]:
        del config_dict["inputs"]

    return config_dict

def validated_graph(
    data: dict, *, collect_errors: bool = False, project_dir: Path | None = None
) -> "MetaworkflowGraph":
    """Construct a MetaworkflowGraph from a raw, parsed-YAML config dict.

    Steps can be declared as a dict keyed by id (`steps: {<id>: {...}}`,
    the preferred form) or in list notation each with an `id` key.
    Transitions, describing directed dependencies in the MetaworkflowGraph
    is defined via `from:` keys in each step definition, where a single id string
    or a list of ids is accepted.

    By default the graph construction fails fast, raising on the first parsing error
    found. For a best-effort pass that collects every problem instead of stopping
    at the first use `collect_errors=True`.

    All paths, unless they are absolute, are interpreted relative to the `project_dir`,
    where the YAML config lives. `project_dir` defaults to the current workdir.

    Deprecations: the old key names `workflows:` (for `steps:`), `config_file` and
    `profile`, the list form of `steps:` and the top-level `transitions:` key are
    still read, with a warning. Automatically fix this by opening and saving the
    config via the editor.

    project_dir = (project_dir or Path.cwd()).resolve()
    if collect_errors:
        return _full_validated_graph(data, project_dir)
    return _fast_validated_graph(data, project_dir)

def validated_workflow(
    data: dict, warnings: list[Diagnostic] | None = None, project_dir: Path | None = None
) -> Workflow:
    """Construct and fully validate a single workflow from a flat, raw dict
    (`id` is optional and will be generated).
    Runs the same tier-0/1 construction plus tier-2 dynamic checks
    a workflow gets as part of a full config build. Returns the validated
    Workflow, or raises `GraphValidationError`/`ConfigValidationError`.

    Warnings are appended to `warnings` when given, else logged. Relative
    `params_file`/`nf_config` are looked up in `project_dir` (default: the
    current directory).
    """
    if not data:
        raise GraphValidationError("No config data provided")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise GraphValidationError(f"Expected a flat mapping, got {type(data).__name__!r}")
    legacy = _legacy_section_warnings(data)
    if warnings is None:
        log_warnings(legacy)
    else:
        warnings.extend(legacy)
    wf, diagnostics = construct_workflow(data, data.get("id", "<unknown>"))
    if wf is None:
        raise ConfigValidationError(diagnostics)
    dynamic_diagnostics = run_dynamic_checks(with_absolute_config_paths(wf, project_dir), previous=None)
    errors = [d for d in dynamic_diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.ERROR]
    found_warnings = [d for d in dynamic_diagnostics if d.severity == Severity.WARNING]
    if errors:
        raise ConfigValidationError(errors, warnings=found_warnings)
    if warnings is None:
        log_warnings(found_warnings)
    else:
        warnings.extend(found_warnings)
    return wf

Abstract base class for all metapipeline runner backends.

Subclasses register themselves by defining a RUNNER_NAME class attribute. The value is the string name used to select the runner::

def build_step_spec(
    wf: Workflow,
    global_options: GlobalOptions | None,
    *,
    state_dir: Path,
    launch_dir: Path,
    work_dir: Path | None = None,
    log_file: Path | None = None,
    nextflow_cache_dir: Path | None = None,
    project_dir: Path | None = None,
    schema: Schema | None = None,
    extra_profile: str = "",
    nf_config: Path | None = None,
    resume: bool = False,
    stub: bool = False,
) -> StepSpec:
    """Combine a step whose references are already resolved with the run's
    globals and locations into a `StepSpec`.

    With a `project_dir`, relative input paths in the step's `params_file` and
    in `globals.params` are made absolute against it (`paths.is_input_path`,
    using `schema`). The step's own params are taken as they are.

    Raises:
        NfMetaRunnerError: if the global config file doesn't exist.
    """
    params_file = getattr(wf, "params_file", None)
    params: dict[str, Any] = dict(load_params_file(params_file)) if params_file else {}
    if global_options and global_options.params:
        params.update(global_options.params)
    if project_dir is not None:
        params = absolutize_input_paths(params, project_dir, schema)
    params.update(wf.params or {})

    profile = getattr(wf, "nf_profile", None)
    profiles: list[str] = []
    if global_options and global_options.nf_profile and not profile:
        profiles.append(global_options.nf_profile)
    if profile:
        profiles.append(profile)
    if extra_profile:
        profiles.append(extra_profile)

    config_files: list[Path] = []
    if global_options and global_options.nf_config:
        global_cfg = Path(global_options.nf_config)
        if not global_cfg.exists():
            raise NfMetaRunnerError(f"Global config file does not exist: {global_cfg}")
        config_files.append(global_cfg)
    if wf.nf_config:
        config_files.append(Path(wf.nf_config))
    if nf_config is not None:
        config_files.append(Path(nf_config))

    return StepSpec(
        workflow=wf,
        params=params,
        profiles=tuple(profiles),
        config_files=tuple(config_files),
        launch_dir=launch_dir,
        work_dir=work_dir,
        state_dir=state_dir,
        log_file=log_file,
        nextflow_cache_dir=nextflow_cache_dir,
        resume=resume,
        stub=stub,
    )

Raises:

Type Description NfMetaRunnerError
