def plan(self, graph: MetaworkflowGraph, resume: bool = False, dry_run: bool = False) -> RunPlan:
    """Resolve every selected step to its spec and command, in DAG order,
    without writing files or running anything. Values the run needs are
    collected first (see `RunOptions.input_mode`); in prompt mode this
    asks for them, even in a dry run.

    Raises:
        NfMetaRunnerError: if values are missing (except in a dry run
            outside prompt mode, where they become placeholders) or
            invalid, if no out dir can be determined, if a config loaded
            from a URL has relative input paths, or if two steps write to
            the same outdir.
    """
    self.out_dir = self._resolve_out_dir(graph)
    project_dir = graph.project_dir
    # params_file/nf_config are read from here on: as absolute paths
    global_options = graph.global_options and with_absolute_config_paths(graph.global_options, project_dir)
    workflows = [with_absolute_config_paths(wf, project_dir) for wf in self._selected_workflows(graph)]
    subset_ids = {wf.id for wf in workflows}

    # Resolved params and step keys per workflow id, seeded from cached runs
    # of excluded workflows
    resolved: dict[str, dict] = {}
    keys: dict[str, str] = {}
    for wf in graph.get_workflows():
        if wf.id not in subset_ids:
            wf = with_absolute_config_paths(wf, project_dir)
            keys[wf.id] = wf.hash()
            cached = self._load_resolved_params(wf)
            if cached is not None:
                resolved[wf.id] = cached

    requests = self._input_requests(graph, workflows, subset_ids, resolved)
    collected = collect(
        requests,
        self.run_options.inputs,
        InputMode(self.run_options.input_mode),
        project_dir=project_dir,
        prompter=self.run_options.prompter,
        dry_run=dry_run,
    )
    input_values = {r.name: collected.values[r.name] for r in requests if not r.is_reference}
    reference_values = {Binding.parse(r.name): collected.values[r.name] for r in requests if r.is_reference}

    planned: list[PlannedStep] = []
    for wf in workflows:
        bound = graph.bound_params(wf.id)
        if bound or input_refs(wf.params):
            wf = wf.model_copy(update={"params": substitute_inputs(wf.params, bound, input_values)})
        overrides = {b.param: v for b, v in reference_values.items() if b.step_id == wf.id}
        if overrides:
            wf = wf.model_copy(update={"params": {**(wf.params or {}), **overrides}})
        schema = param_schema(wf)
        if project_dir is not None and wf.params:
            wf = wf.model_copy(update={"params": absolutize_input_paths(wf.params, project_dir, schema)})
        elif project_dir is None:
            self._reject_relative_inputs(wf, schema)

        # Before references are resolved: other steps' outputs are covered by
        # their step keys, and may not exist yet
        global_params = (global_options.params if global_options else None) or {}
        if project_dir is not None and global_params:
            global_params = absolutize_input_paths(global_params, project_dir, schema)
        input_files = input_fingerprints({**global_params, **(wf.params or {})})
        wf_resolved = resolve_references(wf, graph, resolved=resolved)
        resolved[wf.id] = wf_resolved.params or {}

        upstream = [keys[p.id] for p in graph.predecessors(wf) if p.id in keys]
        key = self._step_key(wf_resolved, global_options, upstream, input_files)
        keys[wf.id] = key
        state_dir = self._state_dir(wf, key)

        spec = build_step_spec(
            wf_resolved,
            global_options,
            state_dir=state_dir,
            launch_dir=self.out_dir,
            work_dir=self.out_dir / "work",
            log_file=state_dir / "nextflow.log",
            nextflow_cache_dir=self._nextflow_cache_dir(wf),
            project_dir=project_dir,
            schema=schema,
            extra_profile=self.run_options.nf_profile or "",
            nf_config=self.run_options.nf_config,
            resume=resume,
            stub=self.run_options.stub,
        )
        planned.append(
            PlannedStep(
                # as configured, with the config files' absolute paths (as its resolved params' cache key)
                workflow=with_absolute_config_paths(graph.get_workflow_by_id(wf.id) or wf, project_dir),
                resolved_params=wf_resolved.params or {},
                spec=spec,
                command=engine_for(spec.workflow_type).build(spec),
                # The step's outdir holds the last run's results, so an older
                # success with this key counts only if no other key ran since.
                skip=resume and self._check_run_success(run_dir=state_dir) and self._last_run_was(wf, state_dir),
            )
        )
    _check_outdirs(planned)
    return RunPlan(
        steps=planned,
        values=dict(collected.values),
        missing=[r.name for r in collected.missing],
    )

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: The nf-meta package ships a browser-based editor for building and changing metapipeline configs visually: steps as a graph, schema-based forms for their params, references and inputs picked from menus, and validation as you edit. Every change is saved to the config file right away, and the history (undo, redo) takes you back to any earlier state.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# start fresh
nf-meta editor

# or open some existing work
nf-meta editor path/to/metapipeline.yaml

nf-meta editor runs the editor's backend, which exposes an api and serves a one-page frontend application that can be accessed from the browser. It tries to open the frontend as a new tab in your local browser automatically. You can always access the editor also by copy-pasting the printed url and token in the address bar of new tab in a local web browser.

The nf-meta editor backend blocks the terminal by listening to requests until you stop it manually Ctrl + C in the terminal or via the Quit editor button in the page's file menu. Every change is gets automatically saved, so nothing is lost either way.

Started without a config, the editor shows a start screen, asking to open a config, pick one of the configs you recently opened, or start a new metapipeline. The list of recent configs is tracked per user in (~/.local/state/nf-meta/recent-configs.json).

A new config, or one opened from a URL (nf-meta editor https://…), asks for a path to save to before your first change. Cancelling leaves the change unsaved and your edit form open.

docs.title: Working with the editor
docs.text:
The graph shows the steps and the flow between them; the sidebar on the right has three tabs. Drag its edge to make it wider.

Steps. One card per step; click a node or a card to open it. A step's form has the pipeline or module (nf-core names and versions are completed from the nf-core catalog), and its params:

  • The params form is built from the pipeline's nextflow_schema.json (or the module's meta.yml): a field per param, with its type, description and allowed values. "Add param" lists the params not set yet, required ones first. Form/YAML switches to editing the params as YAML, with completion and checks for references and inputs.
  • A reference (the blue button next to a param) fills the param from another step's param: pick the step, then the param. The editor adds the edge between the steps when you save. A reference can have text after it, e.g. /samplesheet/samplesheet.csv.
  • An input (the purple button) makes the param a value supplied at run time; see Inputs.
  • More options holds the params file, Nextflow config and profile, the main script and, for pipelines you develop yourself, a local folder instead of the repository (marked "local"; see Developing a pipeline locally).

Problems show at the field they belong to; a change the checks refuse is not saved.

Warnings don't block a change: an old key name, two steps sharing an outdir, a local pipeline, a repository that couldn't be checked. The yellow count in the footer, next to the history, opens the Warnings tab: all warnings about the config, grouped by key. Each step's warnings show as a yellow count on its node: click it to open the tab with that step's warnings marked. Warnings about old key names go away once the editor has saved the file in the current form. Drag the panel's top edge to make it taller.

Inputs. Lists all run-time inputs of the metapipeline, with the params they fill. Hovering an input highlights its steps on the graph. An input's form sets its description, default and rules (type, format, allowed values, …), and the step params it fills: "Add step param" picks the step, then the param, with each param's description, type and default. A choice at the top writes all inputs in the steps' params or all in the inputs: section.

Globals. Settings for every step: Nextflow version, profile and config, and shared params (deprecated, see the config reference).

Fields that take a path (a step's params file and Nextflow config, the global Nextflow config, params and input defaults with a path format) have a folder button that browses the machine running the editor and fills in the absolute path of the file or folder you pick. You can also type the path, relative to the config's folder, or a URL for params and input defaults. Whatever is in the field is saved as it is. outdir has no button: a relative outdir is placed in the run's output folder.

Configs on a cluster?

Run the editor on the cluster and use it in your own browser through an SSH tunnel: see Running the editor on a remote machine.

docs.title: The editor link
docs.text: On start, the editor backend prints a url where the frontend can be reached along with an access token that is regenerated on every startup. It looks like this: Editor running at: http://127.0.0.1:8080/?token=…. The token is saved and resend by the editor on every request, or the editor backend refuses access. This keeps other users of a shared machine (and websites open in your browser) out of your configs. The browser gets the link through a small file only you can read (in $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or ~/.cache/nf-meta/editor, removed when the editor stops), so the token isn't leaked in the process monitor of a shared machine. When the browser runs on a remote machine (VS Code Remote-SSH, dev containers, Codespaces), that file can't be reached. You can start with --no-redirect-file or open the printed link manually.

docs.title: Running the editor on a remote machine
docs.text:
Data and pipelines usually live on a cluster with no access to a display server or a browser. To use the editor there anyway, run its backend on the cluster and connect to it through an SSH tunnel.

On the cluster start the editor backend:

$ nf-meta editor --port 8080
Editor running at: http://127.0.0.1:8080/?token=Xq3…
Started over SSH: to use the editor from your own computer, forward its port there
    ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 alice@login01
(with the host name you log in with), then open the link above in your browser.

On the computer with a browser, run the following command with the host name of your remote machine to start the tunnel:

$ ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 alice@hpc.example.org

You will now be able to visit the printed link in your local browser.

docs.title: VS Code Remote-SSH
docs.text:
In the terminal of a VS Code Remote-SSH window, the port is forwarded automatically. Start the editor with --no-redirect-file, so the link can be opened on your computer's browser:

nf-meta editor --port 8080 --no-redirect-file

docs.title: Editor backends
docs.text: The editor is extensible via plugins in the same way runners are: --editor <name> selects a registered BaseEditor subclass. The one described above is the only one shipped with nf-meta right now and opens by default. See Writing an editor plugin to add a new third-party-editor.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: nf-meta has four subcommand commands. nf-meta <command> --help lists every option.

docs.title: nf-meta validate
docs.text:
nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml
nf-meta validate https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<commit>/metapipeline.yaml

Checks a config without running it, validating its YAML keys, the references between steps, global inputs, and also validates each pipeline against a schema if one exists. The retrieval of the pipeline schema requires a network connection, but will enable confirming urls and verison extist, required params are given, and all params have the correct type. Problems are listed by line and key in the YAML along with an error message.

By passing --scope step or --scope globals only a snippet of YAML can be validated, instead of a whole config.

docs.title: nf-meta run
docs.text:
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml [--resume] [--out DIR] [--input NAME=VALUE ...]

Runs the steps in the order declared by the graph. The main options:

Option Effect --resume Skip steps that already succeeded unchanged; resume Nextflow's tasks for the rest. -o, --out DIR Where to run and write results (default: nf-meta-out in the current directory). -i, --input NAME=VALUE A value for an input (once per value), or <step-id>.<param> for a step outside the run. --inputs-file FILE Input values as a YAML mapping. --input-mode prompt\|fail\|reproduce What to do with values the run needs but doesn't have. -s, --start ID, -t, --target ID Run only the steps from one step to another. --dry-run Print each step's command and params file, run nothing. --stub Pass -stub to Nextflow. -p, --nf-profile, -c, --nf-config A Nextflow profile or config for every step.

See Runners for what each does in detail.

docs.title: nf-meta editor
docs.text:
nf-meta editor [metapipeline.yaml]

Starts the editor and opens it in the browser.

Option Effect --port PORT The port to listen on (a free one if omitted). --host HOST The address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1). --no-browser Do not attempt to open in a browser automatically --no-redirect-file Do not write a redirect file. (e.g. in a remote session) Requires opening the link manually.

docs.title: nf-meta export-schema
docs.text:
nf-meta export-schema [OUTPUT]

Exports the config format's JSON Schema (default: schemas/metapipeline.schema.json) to a file. See Editor autocompletion for how to use it in VSCode.

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
The package is published to the Python Package Index and can be installed with your favorite dependency tool:

# with pip
pip install nf-meta

# as a command-line tool with uv
uv tool install nf-meta

# as a dependency of your project with uv
uv add nf-meta

Note

nf-meta orchestrates Nextflow runs. The PyPI package does not bundle Nextflow, so running a metapipeline (nf-meta run) requires a working installation on PATH. Steps of type nf-module need Nextflow 26.04 or later (nextflow module run). Validating a config (nf-meta validate) and the editor (nf-meta editor) don't need Nextflow.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text: See Contributing → Development setup for installing from a clone and running the editor in dev mode.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This example shows you the smallest metapipeline possible, consisting of just one step. It only executes the nf-core/fetchngs pipeline to fetch some data from a public repository. The resulting metapipeline is validated and executed via the CLI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• nf-meta installed (see Installation)
  • Nextflow installed, required for nf-meta run but not for the nf-meta validate or editor commands.

docs.title: 1. Write a config
docs.text:
Create metapipeline.yaml:

config_version: 0.5.0
steps:
  fetch:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/test-datasets/2732b911c57e607fa7aea5ba0c3d91b25bafb662/testdata/v1.12.0/sra_ids_test.csv
      outdir: results
  • config_version pins the representation's schema version. See Config reference.
  • fetch is the step's id. Other steps reference it (see Cross-step references), and --start/--target select it on the command line.
  • name/version uniquely describe an nf-core pipeline. For a non-nf-core pipeline, the url field is required as well.

docs.title: 2. Validate it
docs.text:
nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml

During validation, first the config shape is checked statically for required keys, references, and graph layout. The config's static shape is also available as a JSON Schema your editor can check as you type. (See Editor autocompletion) Next, nf-meta tries to incorporate metadata provided by nf-core as well as in each pipeline's nextflow_schema.json file to validate urls, versions, and required parameters or types. You will get summarized validation feedback with line numbers and keys in your console.

docs.title: 3. Run it
docs.text:
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --stub

To just see that everything runs as expected, we use Nextflow's stub-run mechanism which replaces each process script with a no-op stub that requires no containers or environment. This Nextflow run options is resurfaced to the nf-meta run cli interface as the --stub flag. This can be useful to confirm the structure and parameter wiring resolves correctly without waiting on real compute or container pulls.

The results land in nf-meta-out/results/ in the folder you ran nf-meta from: every step runs in the out dir (--out sets another one).

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• A metapipeline with more than one step, chained via references: see YAML representation overview.
  • Editing configs visually instead of by hand: see Editor.
  • Leaving values such as the sample sheet to the person running it: see Inputs.
  • Where results go and how nf-meta run --resume decides what to re-run: see Runners.

docs.title: Writing a runner plugin
docs.text: A runner turns a validated MetaworkflowGraph into actual Nextflow execution. This walks through the minimum needed to add one as an installable plugin. See BaseRunner for the full contract.

docs.title: 1. Subclass BaseRunner
docs.text:
# my_runner_package/runner.py
from nf_meta.core.graph import MetaworkflowGraph
from nf_meta.runner import BaseRunner, RunResults


class MyRunner(BaseRunner):
    RUNNER_NAME = "my-runner"

    def run(self, g: MetaworkflowGraph) -> RunResults:
        for step in g.get_workflows_sorted():
            ...  # execute the step, in dependency order

    def resume(self, g: MetaworkflowGraph) -> RunResults:
        ...  # continue a previous run, skipping what already succeeded
  • RUNNER_NAME is required. Defining it is what registers the class (via BaseRunner.__init_subclass__), and it's the string users pass to --runner.
  • Don't override __init__. self.run_options (a RunOptions) is already set by BaseRunner.__init__; read self.run_options.out_dir, .stub, .start/.target, .inputs, etc. from there.
  • Return a RunResults (one StepResult per step), and let failures raise (NfMetaRunnerError): run_metapipeline doesn't catch exceptions from run/resume, so a step failure should propagate rather than being swallowed into a silent partial result.
  • Optionally implement plan(g, resume, dry_run) returning a RunPlan: that is what nf-meta run --dry-run prints. Without it, a dry run with your runner says it isn't supported.

To run steps with Nextflow the way the built-in runner does, reuse its pieces: nf_meta.runner.spec.build_step_spec turns a step (with references resolved) into a StepSpec (params, configs, profiles, launch and work folders), and nf_meta.runner.engines.engine_for( step.type).build(spec) gives the StepCommand (argv, folder, environment) to execute.

docs.title: 2. Advertise it as a plugin
docs.text:
Registration only happens when the module defining MyRunner is actually imported. nf-meta discovers runner plugins via the nf_meta.runners entry-point group. Add this to your package's pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."nf_meta.runners"]
my-runner = "my_runner_package.runner:MyRunner"

Once installed alongside nf-meta, my-runner appears in nf-meta run --runner without any change to nf-meta itself.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
pip install -e .   # or however your plugin package installs
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --runner my-runner

If it doesn't show up, check that the entry point's module actually imports without error. _load_runner_plugins logs a warning (not a hard failure) and skips a plugin that fails to load, which can silently hide a broken import.

docs.title: Writing an editor plugin
docs.text: An editor backend is what nf-meta editor --editor <name> launches. This walks through adding one as an installable plugin. See BaseEditor for the full contract.

docs.title: 1. Subclass BaseEditor
docs.text:
# my_editor_package/editor.py
from nf_meta.editor import BaseEditor


class MyEditor(BaseEditor):
    EDITOR_NAME = "my-editor"

    def start(self) -> None:
        ...  # block until the user is done editing
  • EDITOR_NAME is required. Defining it registers the class (via BaseEditor.__init_subclass__) and is the string users pass to --editor.
  • Don't override __init__. self.options (an EditorOptions) is already set; read self.options.host/.port from there if your backend serves over HTTP.
  • start() should block until the user is finished (the built-in BrowserEditor runs its server synchronously in the calling thread). It isn't expected to return while editing is still in progress.

docs.title: 2. Advertise it as a plugin
docs.text:
nf-meta discovers editor plugins via the nf_meta.editors entry-point group:

[project.entry-points."nf_meta.editors"]
my-editor = "my_editor_package.editor:MyEditor"

Once installed alongside nf-meta, my-editor appears in nf-meta editor --editor without any change to nf-meta itself.

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
pip install -e .   # or however your plugin package installs
nf-meta editor --editor my-editor metapipeline.yaml

As with runner plugins, a plugin module that fails to import is skipped with a logged warning rather than a hard failure. Check that first if my-editor doesn't show up as a choice.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: An input is a value that can be supplied at the time of running the metapipeline, such as the sample sheet, a genome, a contrasts file. Inputs keep those values out of the step definitions, so the same metapipeline config runs on new data without editing it. nf-meta run asks for them (optionally prompting for them), and the editor displays them in its Inputs tab.

docs.title: Global and implicit inputs
docs.text:
An input can fill one or more step params and there are two ways to define them. Use only one of them per input.

Implicitly in the step's params, with ${inputs:<name>} instead of writing the value:

steps:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: ${inputs:ids}
      outdir: out_fetchngs

This declares the input ids on the spot. It gets its type, format and description from the param it fills (input in fetchngs's schema: a file-path that must exist).

The second way is in the inputs: section, with bind: listing <step-id>.<param>:

inputs:
  ids:
    description: SRA ids to fetch, one per line
    bind: [n01.input]
steps:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      outdir: out_fetchngs

Both describe the same thing. The inputs: section keeps all run-time values in one place at the top of the config, whereas the params notation keeps them inside the respective step. The editor can move all inputs from one form to the other.

Whichever method is chosen, the input declaration will fill the whole param value and cannot be embedded in a string, the way a step reference can.

An input may also be declared in inputs: without bind: and referenced with ${inputs:ids} in params. The declaration can then be used to add a description, a default or schema rules. But an input with bind: cannot also be referrenced with ${inputs:...}.

Several params can reference the same input and will all get its value, but an unreferenced input leads to a warning.

See also inputs: keys reference.

docs.title: Supplying values when running
docs.text:
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --input ids=ids.csv --input genome=GRCh38
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --inputs-file values.yaml   # a YAML mapping of name: value

Inputs specified in the metapipeline config, but not supplied via the CLI, are handled according to --input-mode:

--input-mode Missing values Given values prompt (default in a terminal) asked for before the first step, with selection lists, path completion and checks as you type used fail (default otherwise) the run stops and lists them used reproduce the run uses exactly the values of the last run refused

Every value is checked against the input's rules before anything runs, and all problems are reported together. Relative paths given on the command line are relative to the current folder, as usual for a command; defaults written in the config are relative to the config's folder.

See Resume for how inputs impact re-runs.

docs.title: Step references
docs.text:
A param value can read the value of another step's param with a construct like this:

${<step-id>:<namespace>:<key>}

Here,

  • <step-id> is the id of another step under steps: in the same config.
  • <namespace>: only params is supported currently.
  • <key> is the referenced step's param name.

For example, samplesheet: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv reads the param outdir from the step n01 and uses it to construct the value of samplesheet at run time.

Each param value can reference and read from only one other param in a predecessor step. A value containing two references is an error. To expose a param value as a metapipeline input instead, use an input: ${inputs:<name>}.

docs.title: The flow between steps
docs.text: A reference requires a directed edge from the referenced to the referencing step. Steps declare their predecessors with from:, and a reference to a step that isn't upstream is an error. The editor and the Python API add the needed from: entries when a step is saved, so you only pick the reference. A reference that would create a cycle is refused.

docs.title: Resolution at run time
docs.text:
References are resolved in string params only, just before the referencing step runs, from the value the referenced step ran with. A reference to an upstream outdir stays relative, so it points into the run's output folder where that step wrote its results.

When only part of a metapipeline runs (--start/--target), a reference to a step outside the run takes the value from that step's last run. If there is none, the run asks for it, or takes it from --input <step-id>.<param>=<value> (see Running part of a metapipeline).

docs.title: YAML representation overview
docs.text:
The nf-meta toolkit allows representing a metapipeline of individual Nextflow pipeline or module steps, as a single .yaml file. The top-level keys of the YAML are:

  • config_version pins the format this document follows, so the representation can evolve without breaking older configs. See Config reference for the supported range.
  • steps is a mapping of step id to step definition. Each step is one Nextflow pipeline or module run. The flow between steps is declared per step via from:. (Configs from before 0.5.0 call this key workflows; it is still read, see Old key names.)
  • globals holds settings applied to every step (Nextflow version, profile, shared params, ...).
  • inputs declares values supplied when the metapipeline runs, such as the sample sheet. See Inputs.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
config_version: 0.5.0
globals:
  nextflow_version: "25.10"
steps:
  n01:
    name: nf-core/fetchngs
    version: 1.12.0
    params:
      input: ${inputs:fetchngs_ids}
      outdir: out_fetchngs
      nf_core_pipeline: rnaseq
      nf_core_rnaseq_strandedness: auto
  n02:
    from: n01
    name: nf-core/rnaseq
    version: 3.14.0
    params:
      input: ${n01:params:outdir}/samplesheet/samplesheet.csv
      genome: GRCh38
      outdir: out_rnaseq

Step n01 runs the nf-core/fetchngs pipeline first, reading its samplesheet via an input declaration. The step n02 (nf-core/rnaseq) runs after n01 (nf-core/fetchngs) as ordered by the from: n01. It reads reads its input from n01's own outdir param via the reference ${n01:params:outdir}. See Cross-step references for the full syntax. A reference is checked topologically, and against both pipeline's metadata, if a nextflow_schema.json can be accessed.

docs.title: Configs from a URL
docs.text:
nf-meta run and nf-meta editor also take a config's URL, so a published metapipeline runs without downloading it first:

nf-meta run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/<commit>/metapipeline.yaml

A config from a URL has no folder of its own, so:

  • relative params_file/nf_config paths in it are an error (use absolute paths, download the files, or make them inputs);
  • the editor never writes back to the URL. Before the first change, the editor asks to save the metapipeline locally.

docs.title: Developing a pipeline locally
docs.text:
While you write a pipeline of your own (for example a small connector between two nf-core pipelines), a step can run it from a local folder with path: instead of url: and version::

steps:
  n02:
    name: fetchngs2rnaseq
    path: ../pipelines/fetchngs2rnaseq   # relative to this config's folder
    from: n01

nf-meta runs nextflow run <folder> and reads the param schema from the folder's nextflow_schema.json. The folder must hold main.nf (or the step's main_script, see below). With --resume, a change to the pipeline's files re-runs the step.

Not reproducible

A config referencing a local pipeline only runs where that folder exists and its code can change between runs, so validate, run and the editor always warn about it. To share the metapipeline, publish the pipeline to a public repository described with url: and version:.

docs.title: Several pipelines in one repository
docs.text:
One repository can hold several pipelines, for example small connectors between steps, each in its own folder. A step picks one with main_script, relative to the repository's root (or to the path folder):

steps:
  n02:
    name: fetchngs2rnaseq
    url: https://github.com/my-org/connectors
    version: 1.0.0
    main_script: connectors/fetchngs2rnaseq/main.nf
    from: n01

Nextflow then treats the script's folder as the pipeline. Each folder needs everything a pipeline needs, in that folder:

  • nextflow_schema.json: nf-meta checks the step's params against this file and the editor builds its form from it. A schema at the repository's root is not used.
  • nextflow.config, if the pipeline needs one. The root's nextflow.config (and its manifest) is not read.

docs.title: Validating and running
docs.text:
nf-meta validate metapipeline.yaml   # static + schema checks
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml        # executes the chain in dependency order, requires Nextflow

As the name indicates, nf-meta validate checks the correctness of a metapipeline config. It checks if the YAML shape, i.e. top-level keys described by the schema and individual steps, represented by Pydantic models, parse correctly. It also validates the urls and versions of steps, as well as graph topology, references and input declarations. Where available, the pipeline metadata in the form of nextflow schemas is used to further validate the individual param declarations.

See the quickstart for a minimal end-to-end walkthrough, and Runners for more information

docs.title: Editor autocompletion (JSON Schema)
docs.text:
nf-meta publishes a JSON Schema for static checks of the config format. It can be used to drive inline validation and autocomplete in editors that support the yaml-language-server schema convention.

The schema only covers the config's static shape: Top-level keys, per-workflow fields like name/version/from, required-ness, types. Since nf-meta describes a structurally flexible declaration format, the schema has no way to know what's valid inside a given workflow's params:.

Any config saved through the editor has the following line added automatically, which enables these static checks in VSCode when using the YAML extension (redhat.vscdoe-yaml): 

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bmds-tue/nf-meta/refs/heads/main/schemas/metapipeline.schema.json
steps:
  ...

To utilize it in VSCode:

  1. Install the YAML extension (redhat.vscode-yaml).
  2. Point the extension at the nf-meta schema: # yaml-language-server: $schema=...
  3. Start typing, see static validation hints, and use Ctrl+Space to auto-complete keys

The schema can be re-generated via an nf-meta installation and the extension be pointed at a local path.

nf-meta export-schema schemas/metapipeline.schema.json

docs.title: Config reference
docs.text: Key-by-key reference for the metapipeline .yaml format. See YAML representation overview for how these fit together, Cross-step references for the ${...} syntax usable in params values, and Inputs for the inputs: section.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text: A relative path in a config (params_file, nf_config, a local pipeline's path, path params and input defaults) is always interpreted as relative to the folder containing the metapipeline config file. This is regardless of where nf-meta is run from with the exception of a step's outdir which is relative to the run's output folder (--out, see Where results go). Paths are kept as written when saved via the editor.

docs.title: Top level YAML keys
docs.text: Key Type Required Default Notes config_version string yes — The format version the config follows, between 0.0.1 and the current 0.5.0. Saving from the editor writes 0.5.0. steps mapping (id → step definition) yes — See Steps below. A list form exists for backward compatibility but is deprecated. globals mapping no none See Globals below. inputs mapping (name → input) no none Values supplied when the metapipeline runs. See Inputs. Requires config_version 0.4.0 or later.

docs.title: Globals
docs.text:
Settings for every step. A step's own settings take precedence over them.

Key Type Required Default Notes nf_profile string no none Nextflow -profile for every step that doesn't set its own nf_profile. Whitespace is stripped. nf_config path to an existing file no none Passed as a Nextflow -c to every step, before a step's own nf_config. params mapping (str → scalar) no none Deprecated, to be removed in a later version: set params per step and declare shared values as inputs. Merged under each step's own params; the step's values win on a key collision. Values must be str/int/float/bool. nextflow_version string, int or float no none e.g. "25.10", "25.10.4-edge", 25. Write it in quotes: unquoted, YAML reads 25.10 as the number 25.1, which is refused. Checked against nextflow -version before a run; a mismatch is reported. Steps of type nf-module need 26.04 or later.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Every entry under steps: is one of two types, selected by type:, nf-pipeline or nf-module. These fields apply to both:

Key Type Required Default Notes (id) — yes — The steps mapping key under the top-level steps:, e.g. n01:. Referenced by from:, ${id:params:key} and the CLI's --start/--target. type nf-pipeline | nf-module no nf-pipeline Selects the pipeline or module fields below. name string, non-empty yes — Pipeline or module name, e.g. nf-core/rnaseq. An nf-core/… name must be in the nf-core catalog; its url and description are filled in from it. version string yes (except for a local pipeline) — A release tag (1.12.0, v1.12.0) or a commit hash. A branch name (dev, master) is rejected, since a reproducible run needs a pinned revision. Use the full 40-character hash: Nextflow 26 can't fetch abbreviated ones (a warning says so). from string or list of strings no none Id(s) of the steps that must finish before this one runs. Saving a step that references another step's params adds the edge it needs. params mapping (str → scalar) no none Passed to Nextflow in a params file. Values must be str/int/float/bool and keep their types. A value may be one step reference (with text after it) or one whole input reference. nf_config path to an existing file no none The step's own Nextflow -c, after globals.nf_config.

docs.title: nf-pipeline steps
docs.text:
For a nextflow run pipeline (the default type):

Key Type Required Default Notes url string for non-nf-core pipelines from the nf-core catalog The pipeline's repository (https://…). For an nf-core pipeline it is filled in from the catalog; a different url is rejected. path path to a folder no none A local pipeline folder, for development, used instead of url and version. See Developing a pipeline locally. Not for nf-core pipelines. description string no from the nf-core catalog Free text. params_file path to an existing .yaml/.yml file no none Base params, merged under params (params wins on a key collision) and included in the params check. nf_profile string no none Overrides globals.nf_profile for this step. main_script string no none Another entry script of the pipeline (-main-script), relative to its root. Nextflow then treats the script's folder as the pipeline: the params are checked against the nextflow_schema.json next to the script, and only that folder's nextflow.config is read, not the root's. The script must exist in the repository at version (checked on github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org). See Several pipelines in one repository. Not for nf-core pipelines.

docs.title: nf-module steps
docs.text:
For a nextflow module run step (Nextflow 26.04 or later):

Key Type Required Default Notes container_engine docker | singularity | conda | podman no none Passed as -with-<engine>. Without it (and without a global nf_config), a warning says the module runs without a container.

Not fully supported yet

Modules can only be run as leaf-nodes in the metapipeline graph at this time. No steps can refernce from a step of type nf-module, yet.

docs.title: Keys of an inputs: entry
docs.text:
Key Notes bind <step-id>.<param> entries the input fills. description Shown in prompts and in the editor. default Used when the run gets no value. A relative path is relative to the config's folder. type string, integer, number or boolean. format For paths: file-path, directory-path, path (a file or a folder) or file-path-pattern (a glob). exists true: a path value must exist. enum The allowed values. pattern A regular expression a string value must match. minimum, maximum Bounds for numbers. mimetype, schema Kept from nf-core schemas, passed through.

Keys you leave out are inherited from the schema of the param the input fills. Keys you set must narrow that schema, never widen it: an enum that picks a few genomes is fine, a type that contradicts the param's is an error. For paths, file-path and directory-path narrow path; declaring path for a param that takes only a file-path is an error. When an input fills several params, their schemas must agree (or one must narrow the other).

docs.title: Key names from previous versions
docs.text:
Configs written for earlier versions still load. Each old form gives a deprecation warning, and saving from the editor writes the current form.

Old Current Since workflows: steps: config_version 0.5.0 config_file nf_config config_version 0.4.0 profile nf_profile config_version 0.4.0 steps: as a list of entries with their own id a mapping keyed by id earlier versions top-level transitions: ({source, target} pairs) each step's from: earlier versions

docs.title: Runners
docs.text: A runner executes a validated metapipeline. nf-meta run --runner <name> selects one (default python); runners are registered BaseRunner subclasses, and other packages can add their own.

docs.title: Python runner
docs.text:
nf-meta run uses the Python runner (--runner python, the default). It runs the steps in dag order from this Python process, each as a nextflow run (pipelines) or nextflow module run (modules) subprocess, and streams their output.

nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml                 # run everything
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --resume        # skip what already succeeded, resume the rest
nf-meta run metapipeline.yaml --dry-run       # print each step's command and params, run nothing

docs.title: Where results go
docs.text:
Every step runs in one out dir: nf-meta-out/ in the folder nf-meta run is started from, or the folder given with --out (relative to that folder too). Paths in the config are still relative to the config's folder. A relative outdir param therefore lands inside it, and references to an upstream step's outdir find its results there.

nf-meta-out/                       every step's Nextflow launch folder
  out_fetchngs/  out_rnaseq/  ...  relative step outdirs
  work/                            Nextflow's work dir (-w), shared by all steps
  .nf-meta/
    steps/<id>_<step key>/         params.yaml, nextflow.log, OUT.txt, ERROR.txt
    nextflow/<id>/                 the step's own Nextflow history and task cache
    inputs.yaml                    the input values of the last run (for --input-mode reproduce)

Give each step its own outdir. nf-meta run refuses two steps with the same outdir, and validate and run warn about an outdir inside another step's. A pipeline step without an outdir param writes wherever the pipeline's own config says, relative to the out dir, so run warns about it too.

With --resume, a step that already succeeded with the same step key is skipped only if no other version of it ran since, because the step's outdir holds the results of its last run.

Relative input paths in params are made absolute against the config's folder before a step runs, so they work from the out dir: a param counts as an input path when its schema declares a path, or when its value names a file or folder that exists in the config's folder. outdir, URLs and references are left alone. See Paths.

A step that fails stops the run: later steps don't start, and the message names the step's folder under .nf-meta/steps/ with its Nextflow log.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
nf-meta run --resume works on two levels.

1. Steps (nf-meta). A step is skipped when it already finished successfully with the same step key. The step key covers everything that defines the step's result:

  • the step as configured, after its references are resolved (name, version, params, …);
  • the content of its nf_config and params_file, and of the global and --nf-config configs;
  • the globals, the --nf-profile and --stub options;
  • the local input files its params name: path, size and modification time (for a folder, those of its entries);
  • for a local pipeline, its files;
  • the step keys of its upstream steps.

So a change to a step re-runs that step and every step downstream of it; steps before it stay skipped.

2. Tasks (Nextflow). A step that does run is started with Nextflow's -resume, against that step's own Nextflow cache (.nf-meta/nextflow/<id>/). Nextflow then reuses every task whose script and inputs are unchanged. A step that failed at task 10 of 15, run again after a fix, only redoes the tasks the fix affects.

What resume can't see:

  • files named inside an input file (e.g. the FASTQ files listed in a sample sheet) and files named in a params_file; only the sample sheet or params file itself counts;
  • remote inputs (https://, s3://);
  • tasks across steps: each pipeline is one unit for nf-meta. After an upstream step re-ran, Nextflow can only reuse a downstream task when its input files are unchanged, which is rare.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Values for the config's inputs come from --input name=value (once per value), --inputs-file values.yaml, an input's default, or a prompt. All of them are collected and checked before the first step runs. --input-mode decides what happens with missing ones: prompt (ask; the default in a terminal), fail (stop with a list; the default otherwise), or reproduce (use exactly the values of the last run).

A changed input value changes the step key, so the steps it reaches re-run.

docs.title: Running part of a metapipeline
docs.text: --start <id> and --target <id> run only the steps between two steps (inclusive). A step inside the selection that references a step outside it takes that value from the other step's last run. If it never ran, the value is asked for like an input, or given as --input <step-id>.<param>=<value>. With --input-mode reproduce, the steps outside must have run before.

docs.title: Other options
docs.text:
Option Effect --out DIR The out dir (default: nf-meta-out in the current directory). --dry-run Print each step's command and params file without running anything. In prompt mode it asks for missing values, so the commands are the real ones; otherwise missing values show as placeholders. --stub Pass -stub to Nextflow: each process runs its stub instead of its script, to check the wiring without real compute. --nf-profile, -p A Nextflow profile for every step, after the configured ones. --nf-config, -c A Nextflow config for every step, taking precedence over the global and step configs. --output-lines, -l How many lines of each step's output to show while it runs.

globals.params are merged under each step's own params (the step's values win).

docs.title: Planned
docs.text:
• nf-cascade runner: compile the config into a single daisy-chained Nextflow script, delegating orchestration to nf-cascade. A stub (NfCascadeRunner) exists in the codebase but is not yet implemented.
  • Seqera Platform runner: start and monitor runs by calling a Seqera Platform instance's API with the resolved parameters, rather than shelling out to nextflow locally.
  • Meta-pipeline runner: compile the config into a monolithic Nextflow project that imports the required workflows directly, for the most efficient orchestration and graceful cross-workflow error handling.
  • Notebook runner: transpile the meta-pipeline config into its most interactive form: A Jupyter notebook moving the Workflow runs closer to your downstream analysis.

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text: Runners are pluggable via the same entry-point mechanism as third-party packages: a package registers a BaseRunner subclass under the nf_meta.runners entry-point group, and it becomes selectable via --runner <name> as soon as it's installed, with no changes to nf-meta itself. See Writing a runner plugin.
